purpose: Paired loopback runs on application-shaped fixture profiles. Loopback timings support relative comparison of scheduling behavior only, not an Internet speed claim. Packet loss is not emulated.

tools.curl: curl 8.21.0 (Windows) libcurl/8.21.0 Schannel zlib/1.3.2 WinIDN WinLDAP

measurement.order: per repetition and profile, clients shuffled with a seeded PRNG (--seed)
measurement.timeToVerifiedMs: wall time of the tool process plus a SHA-256 pass over its output file after it exits; Chrome uses cold browser startup through native download completion and shutdown

chrome.mode: native download via Page.navigate and Browser.downloadProgress completed
chrome.isolation: new profile, disk cache and download directory for every run; extensions disabled
chrome.timing: cold browser spawn through native download completion and browser shutdown; independent SHA-256 follows
chrome.cache: Network.setCacheDisabled plus a fresh disk cache for each run
chrome.cpuAndMemory: not collected: Chrome uses multiple subprocesses

measurement.engineWarmup: fetchpath-cli engine is started before fixture measurements; Chrome starts cold on every run, so startup scopes differ
measurement.cpuAndMemory: user+kernel CPU seconds and peak working set of the directly spawned process, polled every 20 ms from a PowerShell observer; child processes and a separate engine process (fetchpath-cli) are not included
measurement.probe: GET of a tiny endpoint every 100 ms while the tool runs; fixture probe is a separate listener in the fixture worker thread
measurement.interval: median with a seeded percentile bootstrap 95% interval (2000 resamples), reported from 3 runs up; with few runs it understates the real uncertainty

limits: fetchpath-http and fetchpath-cli use TransferLimits::default(): stream-first scheduler, claims sized 1.5 s of lane rate with a 1 MiB floor, 2 lanes to start and 4 at most, 8 active requests, one receive buffer per lane; the engine applies max_connections only when a rule sets it
